plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a two-lens telescope system consisting of a convex objective lens (lens 1, on the left) and a concave eyepiece lens (lens 2, on the right), with the distances f1 and f2 indicated by horizontal brackets beneath the optical axis. Two parallel input rays enter from the left at a small angle δᵢ relative to the optical axis; lens 1 bends them toward the objective focal point to the right of lens 2, and lens 2 then diverges the rays so they exit as a parallel bundle at a larger angle δₒ. The blue vertical marker d shows the offset of the shared focal point from the optical axis in the shown Galilean afocal geometry, where the objective focal point aligns with the eyepiece focal point. This figure demonstrates how a Galilean-style telescope achieves angular magnification equal to the ratio f1/f2 by manipulating ray angles through the two-lens arrangement.

interactionPlan.concept: A Galilean telescope (convex objective + concave eyepiece separated by f1 - f2) is afocal: parallel rays enter at angle δi and leave parallel at angle δo, with angular magnification δo/δi = f1/f2.
elements: horizontal optical axis (blue line) spanning the figure
lens 1: tall convex (biconvex) lens outline at left, blue label 'lens 1' above
lens 2: shorter concave (biconcave) lens outline at right, blue label 'lens 2' above
two parallel input rays (violet/magenta) entering from the left at angle δi to the axis
refracted ray segments between lens 1 and lens 2 converging toward the shared focal point
two parallel output rays (violet/magenta) exiting lens 2 at the steeper angle δo
dashed violet segment from lens 2 to the shared focal point
angle arc + label δi at the left (on each input ray)
angle arc + label δo at the right (on the output bundle)
blue filled dot marking the shared focal point, with a short vertical arrow labeled 'd' showing its offset from the axis
horizontal bracket with end ticks labeled f1 (from lens 1 to the shared focal point)
horizontal bracket with end ticks labeled f2 (from lens 2 to the shared focal point)

interactions.label: Objective focal length f1
interactions.teaches: Lengthening f1 increases the angular magnification f1/f2 and, because the system stays afocal, automatically pushes the lens separation (f1 - f2) and the shared focal point farther right.

interactions.label: Eyepiece focal length f2
interactions.teaches: Shortening the (negative) eyepiece focal length f2 also raises the magnification f1/f2 and pulls lens 2 closer to lens 1, since the afocal separation is f1 - f2.

interactions.label: Input ray angle δi
interactions.teaches: Tilting the parallel input bundle changes δo by exactly the same factor, so the ratio δo/δi stays equal to f1/f2 — magnification is independent of the incoming angle.

interactions.label: Lens 2 offset from afocal position
interactions.teaches: At offset 0 the exit beam is parallel (afocal). Moving lens 2 off the f1 - f2 separation makes the exit rays converge or diverge and shifts the focal-point offset d, revealing that parallel-in/parallel-out holds only at the afocal spacing.

demo_steps.title: Afocal baseline
demo_steps.narration: With lens separation f1 - f2, the objective's rear focal point coincides with the eyepiece's focal point (blue dot, offset d). Parallel rays enter at δi and leave parallel at δo; the readout shows δo/δi = f1/f2.

demo_steps.title: Magnification is angle-independent
demo_steps.narration: Sweep δi: both the input and output bundles tilt together and δo scales in lockstep, so the ratio δo/δi = f1/f2 does not change — the telescope magnifies angle, not a particular ray.

demo_steps.title: Set the magnification with f1/f2
demo_steps.narration: Increase f1 (or decrease f2): the output angle δo grows relative to δi and the readout M = f1/f2 rises, while the lens separation automatically widens to f1 - f2 to keep the system afocal.

demo_steps.title: Break the afocal condition
demo_steps.narration: Move lens 2 off the f1 - f2 spacing: the exit rays are no longer parallel — they converge or diverge — and the focal-point offset d shifts, showing that the clean parallel-in/parallel-out behavior exists only at the afocal separation.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because the afocal spacing f1 - f2 makes the objective's focal point coincide with the eyepiece's, a parallel bundle is mapped to a parallel bundle whose angle is scaled by exactly f1/f2 — that ratio IS the telescope's angular magnification.

Lens 1 is a tall thin biconvex outline near the left third with blue 'lens 1' above; lens 2 is a shorter biconcave outline right of center with blue 'lens 2' above. Two violet/magenta parallel rays enter from the left slightly above the axis at angle δi (small angle arcs + italic δi labels at far left), bend at lens 1 toward the shared focal point, then leave lens 2 as a parallel bundle at the steeper angle δo (italic δo with arc at right). A blue filled dot to the right of lens 2 marks the shared focal point, with a short downward vertical arrow labeled 'd' to the axis and a dashed violet segment from lens 2 to the dot. Below the axis draw two black end-ticked brackets: a long one labeled italic f1 from lens 1 to the focal point, and a shorter one labeled italic f2 from lens 2 to the focal point. authoredPrompt: This figure shows a two-lens telescope system consisting of a convex objective lens (lens 1, on the left) and a concave eyepiece lens (lens 2, on the right), with the distances f1 and f2 indicated by horizontal brackets beneath the optical axis. Two parallel input rays enter from the left at a small angle δᵢ relative to the optical axis; lens 1 bends them toward the objective focal point to the right of lens 2, and lens 2 then diverges the rays so they exit as a parallel bundle at a larger angle δₒ. authoredInteractions:
- Sliders for focal lengths f₁ and f₂: update all ray paths through both lenses and display the angular magnification ratio δₒ/δᵢ = f₁/f₂ in real time, with the lens separation adjusting to maintain the shown Galilean afocal configuration
- Drag the input ray angle δᵢ to change the angle of the two parallel input rays and see the output angle δₒ change proportionally, with ray traces updating through both lenses

authoredContext: A small change in the input ray angle gives a larger change in the output ray angle. The magnification of the telescope is the ratio, $M$, of the angular deviation of an output ray, $\delta_o$, to the angular deviation of an input ray, $\delta_i$.  Writing the focal point offset, $d$, in terms of the rays passing through the centers of lenses 1 and 2 gives the relation, $M = f_1/f_2$, where $f_1$ and $f_2$ are the respective ray focal lengths.

discrepancies: The rendered diagram is squeezed into the left ~45% of the canvas beside a tall control panel, leaving large empty margins top/bottom, whereas the source fills the full width with large, prominent annotations; consequently every label (lens 1/2, δᵢ, δₒ, f₁, f₂, d) reads much smaller than in the source.

In the source the two δᵢ arcs and labels sit cleanly at the left with the upper ray drawn distinctly thicker than the lower; in the render the two δᵢ labels/arcs are cramped against the far-left edge and nearly collide with the ray entry points.

The source places the δₒ arc/label at the far right where the two exit rays are well separated; the render draws it mid-right where the exit rays are still close together, so the output-angle arc is less legible.
evaluation.notes: Optically faithful and physically correct afocal-telescope diagram (convex objective, concave eyepiece, shared focal point with offset d, f₁/f₂ brackets, parallel-in/parallel-out rays, M=f₁/f₂) with four working sliders, a 4-step demo, and tooltips; main weakness is composition — the figure is compressed beside the panel so labels are far smaller and more cramped than the source's full-width layout.
action_items: Give the SVG more horizontal room (e.g. dock the control panel below or narrow it) or reduce the viewbox width so the diagram fills the frame and labels approach the source's prominence.
Shift the δᵢ arcs/labels slightly right and stagger them vertically so they do not crowd the left edge or overlap the ray entry points.
Move the δₒ arc and label further right (larger xc) where the two exit rays have visibly diverged, matching the source's clear output-angle annotation.

feedback.rationale: Overall average of 4.6 with no failure modes, concept and interactivity both at 5, and the remaining issues are minor layout/composition polish that are unlikely to yield meaningful improvement with further iteration.
